title: A Fun Learning Game For Every Age And Subject
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin shares a review game he calls the vocabulary game, designed to build camaraderie and cement information for any subject or grade level. The article lays out a detailed twelve-step procedure: preparing two color-coded sets of alphabet cards, splitting the class into competing groups, adopting a game-show-host persona, and awarding points to teams that correctly and silently spell out vocabulary answers to teacher-given clues. He emphasizes maintaining a lighthearted, theatrical tone throughout, including a genuine game-show voice, while never breaking character. The piece frames the exercise as more than trivia practice, positioning it as a vehicle for teamwork, relationship-building, and shared appreciation among classmates. It closes by describing the deeper purpose behind such games: creating fun and connection in a valued, well-run classroom.
points: The vocabulary game uses two color-coded sets of alphabet cards and competing student groups to review content for any subject or grade level.
Teams must silently and collectively spell out the correct vocabulary word using students each holding a lettered card, racing to finish first.
Full team completion earns 15 points for the winning team and 10 points for the second team, which keeps both teams working to finish.
Adopting an exaggerated, game-show-host persona and never breaking character helps keep the exercise fun without losing structure.
The exercise is intended to build camaraderie and relationships among students, not just to review academic content.
quotes: It’s a review game you can play for virtually any subject and any grade level. And your students will have a blast.
Step #1 – Write each letter of the alphabet on large index cards, one letter per card. Create two sets, one written in red marker and one in blue.
Step #6 – Call two groups up to compete. To begin, each group must stand side-by-side, silent, and facing the room with their hands clasped in front of them.
Step #9 – The first team to have every member holding a card silently while spelling out the word correctly and facing the class gets 15 points.
Step #10 – If the other team is also able to spell the word out correctly, they receive 10 points. This encourages both teams to finish.
Just do so in your host voice and never break character. It’s a time for learning, yes. But it’s also for having fun.
